description: We are All in Space, a team of space and technology enthusiasts ready to go all in on the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We love creative problem-solving and using NASA open data to build something meaningful. We are looking for teammates with skills in programming (Python/JavaScript), data analysis, UI/UX design, research, or storytelling and presentation. Beginners are welcome! If you are curious and committed, join us!

FLAREX – Flame in Freefall

FLAREX is an intelligent platform designed to help researchers explore and understand how flames behave in microgravity environments. It focuses on organizing and analyzing space combustion data, including experimental images and videos, to identify important flame characteristics and visualize scientific findings. By combining data analysis, computer vision, and AI-powered insights, FLAREX aims to make microgravity combustion research more accessible and useful for understanding fire behavior and supporting safer future human space exploration.
details:
FLAREX – Intelligent Microgravity Combustion Analysis and Space Fire Safety Insights Platform

FLAREX is an intelligent scientific platform designed to analyze combustion behavior in microgravity environments and support research into spacecraft fire safety. It addresses the challenges of understanding how flames behave differently in space compared to Earth, where the absence of normal gravity significantly affects flame shape, heat transfer, and combustion processes.

The platform integrates real scientific datasets, experimental images, videos, and research publications, particularly from NASA's Flame Extinguishment (FLEX) experiment. Using computer vision and machine learning techniques, FLAREX analyzes experimental footage, identifies flame regions, extracts visual features, tracks changes over time, and generates measurable indicators of combustion behavior.

It also provides scientific data visualization, experiment comparison, and an AI-powered research assistant that helps users explore experimental results and understand scientific findings through evidence-based explanations with traceable sources.

The project aims to make complex microgravity combustion research more accessible, organized, and understandable, while helping researchers identify patterns and investigate factors affecting flame behavior and extinction. Its ultimate impact is to contribute to a better understanding of fire risks in spacecraft and support the development of safer future space missions.

FLAREX is developed using Python, FastAPI, OpenCV, NumPy, Pandas, and machine learning frameworks, with a modern web interface built using React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. PostgreSQL is used for structured scientific data management.

What makes FLAREX innovative is its integration of scientific data engineering, computer vision, machine learning, experiment comparison, and evidence-grounded AI into one unified research environment. The team prioritizes scientific accuracy, real NASA data, reproducibility, data traceability, and clear communication of research limitations to ensure that generated insights remain scientifically responsible.
